items.description: A deep, steep-sided valley in St. Thomas formed by the Yallahs River, known for its dramatic topography.
facts: Prone to landslides during heavy rain
Major source of aggregate and sand
Scenic but rugged agricultural area

items.description: A series of verdant limestone hills in the western parish of Hanover, providing a backdrop to coastal resorts.
facts: Moderate elevation with lush cover
Includes the historic Dolphin Head mountain
Critical watershed for western Jamaica

items.description: A prominent mountain pass and peak in St. Ann, marking the transition from the central plains to the north coast.
facts: Crossed by the main north-south highway
Known for its steep, winding ascent
Elevation of over 2,000 feet

items.description: A rugged limestone upland area in St. Catherine, characterized by rocky outcrops and dry forest vegetation.
facts: Part of the southern limestone plateau
Bordering the fertile Rio Cobre valley
Rich in indigenous flora species

items.description: The high-altitude interior of Trelawny, forming the heart of the rugged and inaccessible Cockpit Country.
facts: Classical cockpit karst landscape
Extremely difficult terrain to navigate
Major sanctuary for endemic wildlife

items.description: The 'Garden Parish' is defined by these rolling limestone hills, which feature numerous waterfalls and underground rivers.
facts: Source of the famous Dunn's River Falls
High concentration of bauxite mines
Cooler climate than the coastal plains

items.description: A fertile valley region in central Jamaica, supporting diverse agricultural production including citrus and cocoa.
facts: Enclosed by the central mountain ranges
Rich alluvial soil deposits
Hub for rural farming communities

items.description: A high-altitude limestone plateau in central Jamaica, known for its red bauxite soil and temperate climate.
facts: Average elevation of 2,000 feet
Center of the island's bauxite industry
Home to the town of Mandeville

items.description: The 'breadbasket' of Jamaica, consisting of flat, fertile alluvial plains that support intensive vegetable farming.
facts: Drier climate than the northern coast
Bordered by the Santa Cruz Mountains
Utilizes extensive irrigation systems

items.description: A prominent limestone ridge on the southern coast of Clarendon, extending into the Caribbean Sea.
facts: Home to the Portland Point Lighthouse
Features rare dry forest ecosystems
Southernmost point of the island

items.description: A dry, rugged limestone region near Kingston, known for its unique xerophytic vegetation and endemic iguanas.
facts: One of the last pristine dry forests
Home to the endangered Jamaican Iguana
Popular for its nearby seafood beaches

items.description: A significant peak in the western part of the island, offering a commanding view of the surrounding agricultural lands.
facts: Located in the parish of Westmoreland
Part of the western limestone range
Surrounded by sugar cane plantations

items.description: The northern slopes of Jamaica's highest peak, characterized by extremely high rainfall and dense tropical cloud forest.
facts: Steeper than the southern approach
Crucial for the island's water cycle
Inaccessible except via rugged trails

items.description: A rugged limestone mountain range in central Clarendon, historically significant as a refuge for Maroons.
facts: Contains numerous hidden caves
Rich in bauxite and limestone
Heavily forested interior terrain
